junior2024.title: KEP Junior Algorithmics 2024
junior2024.summary: Two online qualifiers and an on-site final in Khorezm. Competition rounds, prizes and results.
junior2024.eligibility: The event was organised for participants who were school students during the 2023–2024 academic year.

eligibility.title: For school students
eligibility.body: Final prizes were divided into grades 5–9 and grades 10–11. Official participation required completing the registration form.

selection.title: Two opportunities to qualify
selection.body: The first qualifier selected 25 finalists, and the second selected another 15. Participants already qualified competed unofficially in the second round.

scoring.title: ACM20M scoring
scoring.body: More solved problems ranked first, with lower penalty breaking ties. Both qualifiers and the final lasted three hours.

fairPlay.title: Independent solutions
fairPlay.body: Submissions were checked for plagiarism. Announcements, problems and standings remain available in the KEP.uz archive.

revo2025.title: REVO CUP 2025
revo2025.context: REVO DAY · REVO Global’s fifth anniversary
revo2025.summary: REVO CUP 2025 brought together competitive programming and cybersecurity. Explore its online qualifiers, Urgench finals, prizes and results.
revo2025.fundNote: The combined fund for competitive programming, CTF and special awards.
revo2025.eligibility: Students, school pupils, developers and cybersecurity enthusiasts competed individually.

tracks.title: CP and CTF
tracks.body: Competitive programming focused on algorithms, while CTF covered cybersecurity tasks. Each track had its own qualifier and final.

selection.title: Top 40 in each track
selection.body: Qualifiers ran online on KEP.uz. Each track selected 40 finalists, and one participant could compete in both finals.

scoring.title: Scoring by track
scoring.body: CP used ACM scoring. CTF awarded points for tasks. The complete final order is available in each track’s standings.

fairPlay.title: Individual competition
fairPlay.body: AI assistance, code sharing and flag sharing were prohibited. Organisers reviewed submissions and disqualified rule violations.

tracks.cp: Algorithmic problems, ACM scoring and 40 places in the Urgench final.
tracks.ctf: Cybersecurity tasks, flags and a separate final for the Top 40.

revo2026.title: REVO CUP 2026
revo2026.summary: Two online qualifiers and a final in Urgench on 12 December. 100,000,000 UZS in main prizes and special awards.
revo2026.fundNote: 84,000,000 UZS for the Top 20 and 16,000,000 UZS for special awards.
revo2026.eligibility: An individual competition using ACM (ICPC) scoring. The Top 120 finalists must attend the on-site final in Urgench on 12 December.

firstBlood.title: First Blood
firstBlood.body: 500,000 UZS for each of the 12 final problems. The earliest accepted solution outside the Top 20 wins.

female.title: Best Female Coder
female.body: The highest-ranked female finalist outside the Top 20.

youngest.title: Youngest Rising Star
youngest.body: The youngest finalist with at least one AC. Equal birth dates are resolved by higher final rank.

veteran.title: Veteran Coder
veteran.body: The oldest finalist with at least one AC. Equal birth dates are resolved by higher final rank.

solution.title: Best Solution
solution.body: Judges choose an accepted solution to J, K or L based on algorithmic complexity, runtime, memory and code quality.

lastMinute.title: Last Minute Hero
lastMinute.body: The finalist gaining the most places through an AC during 16:15–16:30.

persistent.title: Persistent Coder
persistent.body: The finalist who reaches AC after the most failed attempts on one problem. Artificial submission spam leads to disqualification.

scoring.title: More ACs rank higher
scoring.body: Participants are ranked first by solved problems. Equal solve counts are decided by lower total penalty.

penalty.title: 20 minutes per penalised attempt
penalty.body: For each solved problem, add its acceptance minute and 20 minutes for each earlier penalised attempt. Unsolved problems add no penalty.

compilation.title: Compilation Error exemption
compilation.body: Submissions returning CE do not incur the 20-minute penalty.

freeze.title: Standings freeze at 16:00
freeze.body: Submissions in the final 30 minutes are hidden from the public standings. Results are revealed during the 16:30–19:00 closing ceremony in the sports hall.

fairPlay.title: Independent work and plagiarism checks
fairPlay.body: Code sharing, communication with other contestants and external assistance are prohibited. Generative AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude and Copilot are not allowed. MOSS / AST analysis checks submissions.

identity.title: Identity verification at the final
identity.body: Bring a passport or ID card to the 13:00–13:30 briefing. Profile information must match the identity document.

payment.title: Payment within five banking days
payment.body: After results are approved, prizes are transferred to winners’ bank cards or accounts within five banking days. Applicable taxes are withheld.

appeal.title: Questions and appeals
appeal.body: Submit technical and judging appeals through Clarifications during the contest. The organising committee and chief judges decide cases not covered by the regulations.

opening.title: GDG Urgench DevFest opening and keynote sessions

briefing.title: Lunch, identity checks, room allocation and technical briefing
briefing.place: Seminar rooms in the teaching building

competition.title: On-site final · 12 problems · freeze at 16:00
competition.place: Seminar rooms in the teaching building

awards.title: Closing ceremony, standings unfreeze and awards
